```{r libraries}
if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pacman")
}
pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse,  # covers dplyr, ggplot2, lubridate, tidyr, stringr, purrr, forcats
  janitor,    # data hygiene (clean_names, tabyl)
  skimr,      # broad EDA summary
  naniar,     # missingness patterns
  glue,       # string interpolation
  caret
)

merged_df <- read.csv('data/merged.csv')
```

# 0. Cleaning the merged dataset

```{r missing-data}
miss_summary <- naniar::miss_var_summary(merged_df) |>
  mutate(pct_miss = paste0(round(as.numeric(pct_miss), 3), "%"))
print(as.data.frame(miss_summary), row.names = FALSE)

```

Since imputation is outside our scope, we can drop rows before the train test split.

```{r}
# 3. Drop rows containing missing values
clean_df <- merged_df |> drop_na()

# 4. Impact Assessment: Compare key portfolio metrics Before vs. After
b_rows <- nrow(merged_df)
a_rows <- nrow(clean_df)

b_exp  <- sum(merged_df$policy.Exposure)
a_exp  <- sum(clean_df$policy.Exposure)

b_clm  <- sum(merged_df$n_claims)
a_clm  <- sum(clean_df$n_claims)

b_freq <- b_clm / b_exp
a_freq <- a_clm / a_exp

b_loss <- sum(merged_df$total_losses)
a_loss <- sum(clean_df$total_losses)

b_pp   <- b_loss / b_exp
a_pp   <- a_loss / a_exp

b_sev  <- b_loss / b_clm
a_sev  <- a_loss / a_clm

impact_summary <- tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Policy Count (Rows)",
    "Earned Exposure (Years)",
    "Claim Count (N)",
    "Total Incurred Loss ($)"
  ),
  Before = c(
    format(b_rows, big.mark = ","),
    format(round(b_exp, 1), big.mark = ","),
    format(b_clm, big.mark = ","),
    paste0("$", format(round(b_loss), big.mark = ","))
  ),
  After = c(
    format(a_rows, big.mark = ","),
    format(round(a_exp, 1), big.mark = ","),
    format(a_clm, big.mark = ","),
    paste0("$", format(round(a_loss), big.mark = ","))
  ),
  Change = c(
    format(a_rows - b_rows, big.mark = ","),
    format(round(a_exp - b_exp, 1), big.mark = ","),
    format(a_clm - b_clm, big.mark = ","),
    paste0("-$", format(round(b_loss - a_loss), big.mark = ","))
  ),
  Pct_Retained = c(
    paste0(round(a_rows / b_rows * 100, 2), "%"),
    paste0(round(a_exp / b_exp * 100, 2), "%"),
    paste0(round(a_clm / b_clm * 100, 2), "%"),
    paste0(round(a_loss / b_loss * 100, 2), "%")
  )
)
remove(a_clm, a_exp, a_freq, a_loss, a_pp, a_rows, a_sev,
       b_clm, b_exp, b_freq, b_loss, b_pp, b_rows, b_sev)
impact_summary

cat(
"There is negligible Data loss, eliminating only 2.92% of the portfolio."
)

```

Confirm there are no missing values

```{r}
miss_summary <- naniar::miss_var_summary(clean_df) |>
  mutate(pct_miss = paste0(round(as.numeric(pct_miss), 3), "%"))
print(as.data.frame(miss_summary), row.names = FALSE)

df <- clean_df
```

# 1. Perform the Train/Test Split

```{r}
set.seed(42)
train_index <- createDataPartition(df$total_losses, p = 0.70, list=FALSE)
```

```{r}
train <- df[train_index,]
test <- df[-train_index,]
```

```{r}
dim(train)
dim(test)
```

Validate the split, to verify that both train and test data sets have similar distributions across key variables so that neither set is significantly different from each other.

```{r}
bind_rows(
  train |> summarize(set="train", mean_losses=mean(total_losses), pct_zero=round(mean(total_losses)*100, 2)),
  test |> summarize(set="test", mean_losses=mean(total_losses), pct_zero=round(mean(total_losses)*100, 2)),
)
```

```{r}
bind_rows(
  train |> summarize(set="train", mean_exposure=mean(policy.Exposure), pct_zero=round(mean(policy.Exposure)*100, 2)),
  test |> summarize(set="test", mean_exposure=mean(policy.Exposure), pct_zero=round(mean(policy.Exposure)*100, 2)),
)
```

```{r}
validate_split <- function(column) {
  bind_rows(
    train |> count({{column}}) |> mutate(set="train", pct= round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2)),
    test |> count({{column}}) |> mutate(set="test", pct= round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2)),
  ) |> relocate(set, .after=1) |> arrange({{column}}, set)
}
validate_split(pet.Type)
validate_split(pet.Group)
validate_split(pet.Gender)
validate_split(owner.Location)
```

```{r}
write.csv(test, 'data/test.csv', row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(train, 'data/train.csv', row.names = FALSE)
```
